chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from his father, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there an Eid for the Muslims other than the day of Friday, and Al-Adha, and Al-Fitr?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the greatest of them in sanctity.' I said, 'And which Eid is it? May I be your sacrifice.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The day in which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) appointed the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said:
Whoever I am his Mawla, Ali is his Mawla.

I said, 'And which day is it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What do you do with the day? Indeed, the year circulates. But it is the eighteenth of Dhi al-Hijjah.' So I said, 'And what is befitting for us to do on that day?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You remember Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, therein with fasting, and worship, and remembrance of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad. For indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) bequeathed to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he should take that day as an Eid. And thus the Prophets (peace be upon them) used to do; they would bequeath to their successors with that, so they would take it as an Eid.'

key_terms.مَنْ كُنْتُ مَوْلَاهُ فَعَلِيٌّ مَوْلَاه: Whoever I am his Mawla, Ali is his Mawla

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 18th of Dhi al-Hijjah in Shia Islam and how should it be observed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the 18th of Dhi al-Hijjah as the 'Greater Eid' (Eid al-Akbar), commemorating the Ghadir Khumm event where the Prophet Muhammad appointed Imam Ali as his successor. It highlights the Shia practice of combining fasting with worship and remembrance, linking this tradition to the precedent set by previous Prophets who designated days for their successors, thereby affirming the continuity of divine leadership (Imamate).
